index_record.dataset_generation_caption: The figure presents a hierarchical diagram illustrating the relationships among four investigated description logics: RDF, EL, DL-Lite, and ALC. The global layout is a directed acyclic graph arranged vertically, with nodes positioned to reflect a subsumption hierarchy. The topmost node is labeled 'ALC', placed centrally at the apex of the structure. Below it, two nodes are positioned side-by-side: 'EL' on the left and 'DL-Lite' on the right. At the bottom, 'RDF' is located directly beneath 'EL'. All nodes are represented as rounded rectangles with a light gray fill and black borders, containing black text centered within them. The font is consistent across all labels, using a standard sans-serif typeface. The diagram uses solid black arrows to indicate directional relationships between the nodes. Each arrow points from a lower-level description logic to a higher-level one, signifying that the lower logic is subsumed by the higher one, as explained in the caption. Specifically, there is an upward arrow from 'RDF' to 'EL', indicating RDF is subsumed by EL. From 'EL', an arrow points upward to 'ALC', showing EL is subsumed by ALC. Similarly, an arrow extends from 'DL-Lite' to 'ALC', indicating DL-Lite is subsumed by ALC. There are no other connections or edges in the diagram. The overall structure forms a V-shaped hierarchy with ALC as the root, EL and DL-Lite as its immediate children, and RDF as a child of EL. The figure is minimalist, with no additional annotations, colors, or background elements beyond the nodes, arrows, and the caption. The caption below the diagram reads: 'Figure 1: Investigated description logics. An arrow indicates that the lower DL is subsumed by the higher DL.' This clarifies the semantic meaning of the arrows, emphasizing the subsumption relationship in the context of description logics.
